answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities produce correlated conflicting attestations, pairwise evidence exposes up to k(k−1)/2 links, so aggregate slashing grows as O(k²), not merely per identity. Whether the accounts are named zephyr, marble, or sonnet, a detected swarm also triggers an exponential multiplier in bonded-capital loss as k increases, making identity splitting an increasingly poor hedge.
